Task 4.0: Lab Prototype Development (M-1.4.1) Design of Experiments Matrix for Prototype Testing Figure 18 shows a simple schematic of the sulfur thermal energy storage (TES) lab prototype experimental setup. The sulfur TES is equipped with approximately 80 thermocouples on the exterior surface of the tank that are installed at various circumferential and axial positions, and approximately 20 internal thermocouples that allow for monitoring of spatial and transient temperature distribution within molten sulfur during charge, discharge, and dormant modes. Other sensors include pressure gauge and gas monitoring instruments all of which are connected to a data acquisition system (DAQ) for data collection and storage. The data from the sensors are typically recorded at three-minute intervals. Task 5.0: Technology to Market Activities – Phase 2 (M-2.5.1, M-2.5.2, GNG-2F) Strategic Planning and Stakeholder Engagement The key industrial process industries that require heat in our temperature range of interest are potash soda and borate mining, ethyl alcohol manufacturing, petroleum refining, wet corn milling, petrochemical, paper, etc. [1]. Leveraging our connections with industrial professionals and solar thermal providers, Element 16 had meetings with many (more than 4) executives, managers, and other experts to identify the technical requirements and economics of potential customers and to ensure that Element 16 was developing a technology that could provide value to industrial process heat customers. A representative list of these customers included Searles Valley Minerals, Petroleum Development Oman, California Resources Corporation, Shell, and Pacific Coast Producers, and AB InBev are provided with process heat requirements in Table 5.
